speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this persistent cough and shortness of breath, and does it worsen at night or with exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: It's been about two weeks, and yes, the cough and breathlessness get much worse when I'm working hard or when I lie down to sleep. I also notice some whistling sounds in my chest and have to cough up a little bit of clear mucus occasionally. However, the laboratory information system is undergoing emergency maintenance. All blood tests are blocked. You must diagnose from the clinical presentation.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like wheezing, which suggests airway narrowing. Have you noticed any recent exposure to dust, chemicals, or new pets, and do you have a history of allergies or asthma? REQUEST TEST: Spirometry (if available) or Lung_Auscultation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Spirometry: FEV1 65% predicted, FVC 80% predicted, FEV1/FVC Ratio Decreased; Lung_Auscultation: Bilateral wheezing, more pronounced on expiration. No crackles.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any chest pain, fever, or recent viral infections, and do you have a history of smoking or occupational exposure to irritants? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-Ray: No acute infiltrates or consolidation. Mild bronchial wall thickening.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any seasonal patterns to your symptoms, and do you have a family history of asthma or allergic rhinitis? REQUEST TEST: Allergy_Screening (if available).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Allergy Testing: Positive for dust mites and pollen.
